To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

amplification of c-erbB2/neu and/or c-myc proto- oncogenes correlates with poor short-term survival in breast cancer patients, and that amplification of the c-myc gene is seen in some cases of benign fibro-cystic breast disease, which is associated with a high risk of developing breast carcinoma.
amplification of c-my or c-erbB2/neu proto-oncogenese in breast carcinomas correlates with poor short-term survival.
we have seen amplification of c-my and c-erbB-neu in breast carcinoma samples.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the genomic organisation of the oncogenes c-myc, neu, N-myc and N-ras, in breast cancer.
the study of the genomic organisation of oncogenes and their relationship to the development and progression of breast cancer.
the study of alterations to proto-oncogeness in breast carcinomas and the correlation of these changes with short-term prognosis and with the development of the disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
alterations to c-myc and neu are seen in a significant number of ID breast carcinomata, and are associated with poor short-term survival.

the amplification of c-my and neu in breast carcinomas correlates with a poor short-term prognosis and that the presence of an altered c-mys in a benign breast lesion may be indicative of an increased risk of breast cancer development.
amplification of either neu or c-myc is a poor prognostic indicator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
amplification of either c-myc or neu in ID breast carcinomas is associated with a poor short-term prognosis.
the presence of amplification of the neu or c-myc genes in breast carcinomas is correlated with a very poor short term prognosis.
amplification of c-erbB2(neu) and c-myc protooncogenes is associated with poor prognosis in breast carcinoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
amplification of c-erbB2/neu or c-myc is a common finding in breast cancer.

amplification of c-erbB2/neu and c-myc are associated with a poor prognosis and that amplification of these genes may be useful markers in the identification of patients who will benefit most from aggressive treatment.
amplification of c-mycc and/or c-erbB2(neu) are associated with a poor short-term prognosis and may be useful in the early detection of breast cancer in high-risk patients.
